subtitle: Where the Silver Tide Met the Saka Road

panels.shot: sweeping aerial over a crowded ancient port at dusk
panels.action: Merchant of Barygaza stands on a busy wharf piled with cotton bales and jars, watching ships ride a swirling tide in the wide estuary below the fortified town of Bharuch under a Saka-era skyline.

dialogue.text: In Nahapana’s time, at Barygaza on the roaring gulf, Saka satraps, inland roads and foreign winds met in silver, cotton and risk.

i18n.hi: नहपान के ज़माने में, गरजती खाड़ी पर बारिगज़ा में साका शासक, ज़मीनी राहें और पराए बयार चाँदी, सूती कपड़े और ख़तरे में मिलते थे।

panels.shot: low, wide shot from ship’s prow entering estuary
panels.action: Merchant of Barygaza stands as a local pilot on a foreign-style ship’s prow, pointing towards the distant town while the vessel rides steep, churning tidal currents in the broad, muddy estuary.

dialogue.text: The Periplus begins with a warning: the approach to Barygaza is perilous, its tides swift, its shoals treacherous, and only local pilots know the safe path upriver.

i18n.hi: पेरिप्लस चेतावनी से शुरू होता है: बारिगज़ा की राह ख़तरनाक है, ज्वार तेज़, रेतीले टीलों में धोखा, और सिर्फ़ स्थानीय नाविक ही नदी की सुरक्षित राह जानते हैं।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Merchant of Barygaza, wind in his hair
panels.action: Merchant of Barygaza grips a rope, steady but alert, as foreign sailors behind him exchange anxious glances, the ship listing slightly while brown water swirls around exposed sandbanks.

dialogue.speaker: Merchant of Barygaza
dialogue.text: Steady your hands. This river has drowned men who thought coin could tame it.

i18n.hi: हाथ सधे रखो। इस नदी ने उन लोगों को भी डुबोया है जो सिक्कों से इसे वश में समझ बैठे।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Bharuch from the river
panels.action: From the river, the fortified town rises above the bank with mud-brick and stone walls, warehouses and temples, while smaller boats dart about and long caravans wait beyond the gate.

dialogue.text: Beyond the tides lies Bharukaccha, Barygaza, a port of the Western Kshatrapas under the Saka satrap Nahapana, where sea routes end and caravan roads begin.

i18n.hi: ज्वार के पार है भरुकच्छ, बारिगज़ा – साका शासक नहपान के अधीन पश्चिमी क्षत्रपों का बंदरगाह, जहाँ समुद्री राहें खत्म होती हैं और कारवाँ के रास्ते शुरू।

panels.shot: interior wide of a bustling warehouse by the river
panels.action: Inside a large riverside godown, Merchant of Barygaza oversees workers stacking bales of fine cotton cloth, jars of sesame oil, bundles of indigo cakes and sacks of rice under wooden rafters.

dialogue.text: The Periplus lists the port’s wealth: cotton cloth from the Deccan, rice from fertile fields, sesame oil and ghee, indigo, onyx and other stones, all gathered in warehouse shade.

i18n.hi: पेरिप्लस बंदरगाह की दौलत गिनता है: दक्खन का सूती कपड़ा, उपजाऊ खेतों का चावल, तिल का तेल और घी, नील, ओनेक्स और दूसरी मणियाँ – सब गोदामों की छाँव में जमा।

panels.action: Merchant of Barygaza’s hands move between piles: he weighs a block of indigo, fingers a fine cotton cloth, then taps a polished onyx bead, as other workers tie bundles with coir rope.

dialogue.speaker: Merchant of Barygaza
dialogue.text: Each bale is a promise—from farmer to weaver to sea and back.

i18n.hi: हर गठरी एक वादा है – किसान से जुलाहे तक, समुंदर तक, फिर वापस।

panels.shot: medium shot of foreign traders entering warehouse
panels.action: Bearded, cloaked foreign merchants with different hairstyles and tunics step into the warehouse, carrying leather bags and small chests, as Merchant of Barygaza turns to greet them with a measured nod.

dialogue.text: From the Red Sea came traders the Periplus calls Yavana, bringing wine in amphorae, copper, tin, lead, coral, and above all gold and silver coin to exchange.

i18n.hi: लाल सागर से आते थे व्यापारी, जिन्हें पेरिप्लस ‘यवन’ कहता है, वे लाते थे घड़ों में शराब, तांबा, राँगा, सीसा, मूँगा, और सबसे बढ़कर सोने-चाँदी के सिक्के सौदे के लिए।

panels.shot: close-up on a spread of coins and goods on a low table
panels.action: On a wooden table, Merchant of Barygaza sets down a folded cotton cloth and a jar of oil as a foreign merchant lays out bright gold and silver coins, coral beads and a small copper ingot.

dialogue.speaker: Merchant of Barygaza
dialogue.text: Your coin buys cloth, oil and colour. But our trust weighs more than metal.

i18n.hi: तुम्हारा सिक्का कपड़ा, तेल और रंग खरीदता है। हमारा भरोसा धातु से भारी है।

panels.shot: wide shot of caravans forming outside city gate
panels.action: Outside Bharuch’s gate, long caravans of ox-carts and pack animals laden with bundled goods line up, with Merchant of Barygaza speaking to a caravan leader while Saka soldiers watch from the walls.

dialogue.text: Barygaza is not only a harbour. It is a hinge. From here, caravans roll inland toward markets and cities whose precise lines the earth has blurred.

i18n.hi: बारिगज़ा सिर्फ़ लंगरगाह नहीं। ये जोड़ है। यहीं से कारवाँ उन अंडराहों की तरफ़ चलते हैं, जिन बाज़ारों और नगरों की रूपरेखाएँ धरती ने धुंधली कर दी हैं।

panels.shot: stylised map-like overhead showing sea and inland routes
panels.action: A stylised scene shows Merchant of Barygaza standing over a sand-drawn map, lines stretching from the Gulf of Khambhat inland to hill regions and beyond, with miniature caravans and ships marking the routes.

dialogue.text: The Periplus names inland centres like Minnagara, their exact locations now debated, reminding us how even trade giants can fade into the mist of argument and guesswork.

i18n.hi: पेरिप्लस अंदरूनी नगरों जैसे मिननगर का नाम लेता है; उनकी सही जगह पर आज बहस है – याद दिलाते कि कभी विशाल मंडियाँ भी बहस और अंदाज़े की धुंध में गुम हो सकती हैं।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of a Saka official at a road post
panels.action: Along a dusty road with trees and a stone cistern, a Saka officer in satrapal attire speaks with Merchant of Barygaza, while travellers rest under a shelter and a carved pillar stands nearby.

dialogue.text: On land, inscriptions of Nahapana’s son-in-law Ushavadata speak of rest-houses, cisterns and gifts along the very routes that feed Barygaza, tying satrap power to merchant roads.

i18n.hi: धरती पर, नहपान के दामाद ऊषवदत्त के लेखों में सराय, पानी के कुंड और दान का ज़िक्र है, इन्हीं राहों पर जो बारिगज़ा को खिलाती हैं, और शासकों की ताकत को व्यापारी मार्गों से बाँधती हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot focused on a stone cistern by the roadside
panels.action: Merchant of Barygaza pours water from a bucket into a traveller’s bowl beside a neatly built stone cistern, as a small inscription panel is visible on the structure’s side.

dialogue.speaker: Merchant of Barygaza
dialogue.text: A full cistern and a shaded bench add more to trade than a drawn sword.

i18n.hi: भरा हुआ कुंड और छायादार चौकी तलवार से ज़्यादा व्यापार बढ़ाते हैं।

panels.shot: interior wide shot of a rock-cut cave monastery
panels.action: Inside a rock-cut cave with pillars and simple cells, monks sit in calm meditation while Merchant of Barygaza and another lay donor stand near a carved inscription on a pillar base.

dialogue.text: Cave inscriptions at places like Nasik record donations from satrap families and merchants, showing how the same wealth that moved along roads also carved stone refuges for the renunciants.

i18n.hi: नासिक जैसे स्थानों की गुफ़ाओं के लेखों में क्षत्रप कुलों और व्यापारियों के दान दर्ज हैं – दिखाते कि इन्हीं राहों से बहता धन सन्यासियों के लिए पत्थर की शरण भी तराशता था।

panels.shot: close-up on carved inscription being traced by fingers
panels.action: Merchant of Barygaza runs his fingers gently over crisp Brahmi letters carved into the rock, his face lit by lamplight as a monk watches with faint approval.

dialogue.speaker: Merchant of Barygaza
dialogue.text: Stone keeps names longer than ledgers. But names too can sink.

i18n.hi: पथ्थर नामों को खातों से ज़्यादा देर थामता है। पर नाम भी डूब सकते हैं।

panels.shot: busy street-level shot inside Bharuch’s bazaar
panels.action: In a narrow bazaar lane, Merchant of Barygaza walks past stalls selling spices, metal tools and dyed cloth, while local buyers and a few foreign traders haggle, children weave between them.

dialogue.text: Himanshu Prabha Ray sees in such ports a web: maritime links, road-side shrines, cave monasteries, all threaded together by merchants who live between wind, tax and trust.

i18n.hi: हिमांशु प्रभा रे ऐसे बंदरगाहों में एक जाल देखती हैं: समुद्री कड़ियाँ, राह किनारे देवालय, गुफ़ा-विहार – सबको जोड़ते व्यापारी, जो हवा, कर और भरोसे के बीच जीते हैं।

panels.shot: evening wide shot on the riverfront with ships at anchor
panels.action: At dusk, Merchant of Barygaza stands on the quay watching ships anchored safely, their masts silhouetted against the sky as the tidal water rises quietly around their hulls.

dialogue.text: As the tide turns gentle and masts darken against the sky, the Periplus notes that this difficult harbour rewards patience, and that satrap rule has made its roads secure enough for risk to seem worth it.

i18n.hi: जब ज्वार नरम पड़ता है और मस्तूलों की परछाइयाँ आसमान पर गहरी होती हैं, पेरिप्लस लिखता है कि यह कठिन बंदरगाह सब्र का फल देता है, और क्षत्रप शासन ने राहें इतना सुरक्षित कर दी हैं कि जोखिम भी क़ीमत के काबिल लगे।

panels.shot: close-up on Merchant of Barygaza holding coins and a ledger
panels.action: Merchant of Barygaza sits cross-legged by lamplight, one hand on a palm-leaf ledger, the other weighing a small pile of mixed coins, some local, some foreign, his face thoughtful.

dialogue.speaker: Merchant of Barygaza
dialogue.text: Today’s silver may come from far seas. Tomorrow’s trust must be earned here.

i18n.hi: आज की चाँदी दूर समुंदरों से आएगी। कल का भरोसा यहीं कमा कर दिखाना होगा।

panels.shot: high, contemplative shot of the port fading into mist over time
panels.action: A time-lapse style view shows the portscape of Bharuch slowly fading into a hazy mist, ships and walls softening as the lone figure of Merchant of Barygaza becomes a silhouette against the river.

dialogue.text: Today the exact paths to places like Minnagara are disputed, yet the record of Barygaza remains: a port where Saka satraps, river pilots and merchants together turned dangerous tides into lasting routes.

i18n.hi: आज मिननगर जैसे नगरों की सही राहों पर झगड़ा है, पर बारिगज़ा का लेखा बचा है – वह बंदरगाह जहाँ साका शासक, नदी के मल्लाह और व्यापारी मिलकर ख़तरनाक ज्वार को स्थायी राहों में बदलते थे।

panels.shot: final medium shot of Merchant of Barygaza on the quay at dawn
panels.action: At pale dawn, Merchant of Barygaza stands alone on the empty quay, looking out as a new ship appears on the horizon, the first light catching his calm, resolute face.

dialogue.text: In the story of Barygaza, we see that trade endures where rulers guard routes, merchants keep faith across cultures, and the hardest currents are faced together, not alone.

i18n.hi: बारिगज़ा की कहानी दिखाती है कि व्यापार वहीं टिकता है जहाँ शासक राहें बचाते हैं, व्यापारी संस्कृतियों के पार विश्वास निभाते हैं, और सबसे तेज़ बहाव अकेले नहीं, मिलकर झेले जाते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: Where the Silver Tide Met the Saka Road
subtitle_i18n.hi: जहाँ चाँदी की लहरें साका सड़क से मिलती थीं
